sections.text:
تستخدم هذه الطريقة لتقدير الرقم الحمضى لزيت العزل والتزييت الروسية الجديدة 
 والمستعملة والمحتوية على اضافات والغير محتوية على اضافات هذه الطريقة تحقق 
 المواصفة القياسية الروسية 
 TOCT 982-56
 .

قام بإعداد هذا المستند الكيميائية/ 
 حنان محمد على حمودة وتم مراجعة المستند 
 بمعرفة الكيميائي/ 
 عبد الناصر محمد الأمين محمود وقامت بالاختبار السيدة الكيميائية/ 
 سهير عبد الوارث حسن وتم اعتماده من الكيميائى/ 
 محمد وجدى عبد الله 
 مدير عام بمحطة كهرباء السد العالى بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء وموثق من المهندس/ 
 عبد النبى عبد الغنى عبد النبى 
 رئيس قطاع المحطة بشركة 
 المحطات المائية 
 لإنتاج الكهرباء.

وهذا المستند معتمد من المهندس/ 
 محمد اسامة سليمان سليم منسق الـMPIS بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء.

rows: تعيين الرقم الحمضى للزيت الجديد لمعرفة مدى مطابقته للمواصفات.

تعيين الرقم الحمضى للزيت المستعمل لمعرفة 
 مدى 
 تأكسد الزيت اثناء التشغيل.
معرفة مدى كفاءة الزيت اثناء التشغيل.

اذابة وزن 
 معلوم من الزيت فى مذيب عضوى (كحول اثيلى) فى وجود دليل روسى (دلتا) ثم 
 معايرة الاحماض المستخلصة من الزيت بمحلول قياسى من هيدروكسيد البوتاسيوم 
 الكحولية.

الرقم 
 الحمضى: هو كمية القلوية معبر عنها بالمللى جرامات من 
 KOH 
 اللازمة لمعايرة الاحماض الموجودة فى 1 جم من عينة الزيت.
التأكد من ان زجاجة العينة جافة (خالية من المياه والاتربة).

يتم اخذ العينة بالطريقة السليمة السالف ذكرها طبقا للـ 
 (MPIS(Oil-013-r2
التأكد من وضع العينة بالصندوق الخاص بها لعدم تعرضها لضوء الشمس والاتربة.
التأكد من صحة البيانات الواردة مع العينة.

التأكد من ان عيارية وتركيز جميع المحاليل والمواد 
 الكيميائية المستخدمة فى التجربة مظبوطة تماما.

وضع المواد الكيميائية المستخدمة فى دواليب جيدة التهوية وفى اماكن بعيدة 
 عن اللهب.

عتد اجراء الاختبار نتجنب اسكاب 
 الزيت على الارض او الميزان وان حدث ذلك يتم ازالته.

ماصة مدرحة 1مل (كل تدريج 0.01 مل) - مكثف عاكس - دورق 250مل - مخبار مدرج 
 100مل - حمام مائى - ميزان حساس.
مذيب عضوى (كحول اثيلى %85 ).
محلول قياسى معلوم (هيدروكسيد البوتاسيوم الكحولى 0.05 عيارى).
دليل دلتا الروسى %0.5 (نيتروسين الاصفر).
نزن 10 جم من الزيت المراد اختباره بدقة فى دورق نظيف وجاف سعة 250مل.

انقل 50 مل من الكخول الاثيلى %85 الى دورق اخر واضف من 4-3 نقط من دليل 
 دلتا الروسى فيصبح لون الخليط اصفر ثم نصل الدورق بالمكثف عاكس.

نضع الدورق المحتوى على الخليط فى 
 حمام 
 مائى والغليان لمدة 5 دقائق.

بعد انتهاء الغليبان يتم معادلة الخليط فى الحال بمحلول هيدروكسيد 
 البوتاسيوم 0.05 عيارى فيتغير اللون من الاصفر الى اللون الاخضر الفاتح.

نضيف الخليط المتعادل على عينة الزيت المراد اختباره ثم نغلى لمدة 5 دقائق 
 اخرى.

بعد انتهاء الغليان نضيف 4-3 
 نقط من دليل دلتا الروسى فنحصل مرة اخرى على اللون الاصفر.

نعاير فى الحال هذا الخليط بمحلول هيدروكسيد البوتاسيوم 
 الكحولى 0.05 عيارى حتى يتغير اللون من الاصفر الى الاخضر الفاتح.

نسجل حجم 
 هيدروكسيد البوتاسيوم المستهلك فى عملية المعايرة.

احسب الرقم الحسابى 
 K 
 من العلاقة

V =
 حجم هيدروكسيد البوتاسيوم الكحولى المستهلك فى عملية 
 المعايرة
 N = 
 عيارية هيدروكسيد البوتاسيوم الكحولى 0.05 عيارى
 G
 = 
 وزن عينة الزيت المراد اختباره بالجرام

sections_en.text: This method is used to determine the acid number of new and used Russian insulating and lubricating oils, with and without additives. This method complies with the Russian standard TOCT 982-56.

This document was prepared by the chemist Hanan Mohamed Ali Hamouda, reviewed by the chemist Abdel Nasser Mohamed El-Amin Mahmoud, tested by the chemist Soheir Abdel Wareth Hassan, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.

rows: Determination of the acid number of new oil to check its conformity with the specifications.
Determination of the acid number of used oil to determine the extent of oil oxidation during operation.
Determining the efficiency of the oil during operation.

Dissolving a known weight of oil in an organic solvent (ethyl alcohol) in the presence of a Russian indicator (Delta), then titrating the acids extracted from the oil with a standard solution of alcoholic potassium hydroxide.
Acid number: the amount of alkali, expressed in milligrams of KOH, required to titrate the acids present in 1 g of the oil sample.
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust).
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2)
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust.
Make sure the data supplied with the sample are correct.
Make sure that the normality and concentration of all solutions and chemicals used in the test are exactly correct.
Place the chemicals used in well-ventilated cabinets, in places away from flames.
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor or on the balance; if this happens, remove it.
Graduated pipette 1 ml (each division 0.01 ml) - reflux condenser - 250 ml flask - 100 ml graduated cylinder - water bath - sensitive balance.
Organic solvent (85% ethyl alcohol).
Known standard solution (0.05 N alcoholic potassium hydroxide).
Russian Delta indicator 0.5% (yellow nitrosine).
Weigh accurately 10 g of the oil to be tested in a clean, dry 250 ml flask.
Transfer 50 ml of 85% ethyl alcohol to another flask, add 3-4 drops of the Russian Delta indicator so that the mixture turns yellow, then connect the flask to the reflux condenser.
Place the flask containing the mixture in a water bath and boil for 5 minutes.
After boiling is finished, neutralize the mixture immediately with 0.05 N potassium hydroxide solution; the colour changes from yellow to light green.
Add the neutralized mixture to the oil sample to be tested, then boil for another 5 minutes.
After boiling is finished, add 3-4 drops of the Russian Delta indicator to obtain the yellow colour again.
Titrate this mixture immediately with 0.05 N alcoholic potassium hydroxide solution until the colour changes from yellow to light green.
Record the volume of potassium hydroxide consumed in the titration.
Calculate the acid number K from the following relation
V = volume of alcoholic potassium hydroxide consumed in the titration; N = normality of alcoholic potassium hydroxide, 0.05 N; G = weight of the oil sample to be tested, in grams

Maintenance Procedures Information System
 | Substations | Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: Oil-015-r0a | Equipment: Standard test method for acidity of petroleum producte (acid number)a
Issued to: High Dam Power Station
Document Status: Approved
Document Approval Date: 18 January 2009 | Procedure: According to russian method (TOCT 982-56)
Date of Next Review: January 2014
Introduction
This method is used to determine the acid number of new and used Russian insulating and lubricating oils, with and without additives. This method complies with the Russian standard TOCT 982-56.
This document was prepared by the chemist Hanan Mohamed Ali Hamouda, reviewed by the chemist Abdel Nasser Mohamed El-Amin Mahmoud, tested by the chemist Soheir Abdel Wareth Hassan, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
Objective
Determination of the acid number of new oil to check its conformity with the specifications. | 
Determination of the acid number of used oil to determine the extent of oil oxidation during operation. | 
Determining the efficiency of the oil during operation. | 
Summary of Method
Dissolving a known weight of oil in an organic solvent (ethyl alcohol) in the presence of a Russian indicator (Delta), then titrating the acids extracted from the oil with a standard solution of alcoholic potassium hydroxide. | 
Definition
Acid number: the amount of alkali, expressed in milligrams of KOH, required to titrate the acids present in 1 g of the oil sample.
Procedures Required for Measurement Accuracy
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust). | 1.
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2) | 2.
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust. | 3.
Make sure the data supplied with the sample are correct. | 4.
Make sure that the normality and concentration of all solutions and chemicals used in the test are exactly correct. | 5.
Environmental Recommendations
Place the chemicals used in well-ventilated cabinets, in places away from flames. | 1.
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor or on the balance; if this happens, remove it. | 2.
Tools and Materials Used
Graduated pipette 1 ml (each division 0.01 ml) - reflux condenser - 250 ml flask - 100 ml graduated cylinder - water bath - sensitive balance. | 1.
Organic solvent (85% ethyl alcohol). | 2.
Known standard solution (0.05 N alcoholic potassium hydroxide). | 3.
Russian Delta indicator 0.5% (yellow nitrosine). | 4.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Test Steps
Weigh accurately 10 g of the oil to be tested in a clean, dry 250 ml flask. | 1.
Transfer 50 ml of 85% ethyl alcohol to another flask, add 3-4 drops of the Russian Delta indicator so that the mixture turns yellow, then connect the flask to the reflux condenser. | 2.
Place the flask containing the mixture in a water bath and boil for 5 minutes. | 3.
After boiling is finished, neutralize the mixture immediately with 0.05 N potassium hydroxide solution; the colour changes from yellow to light green. | 4.
Add the neutralized mixture to the oil sample to be tested, then boil for another 5 minutes. | 5.
After boiling is finished, add 3-4 drops of the Russian Delta indicator to obtain the yellow colour again. | 6.
Titrate this mixture immediately with 0.05 N alcoholic potassium hydroxide solution until the colour changes from yellow to light green. | 7.
Record the volume of potassium hydroxide consumed in the titration. | 8.
Calculations
Calculate the acid number K from the following relation
VxNx56.1 
 ------------------=K 
 G
V = volume of alcoholic potassium hydroxide consumed in the titration; N = normality of alcoholic potassium hydroxide, 0.05 N; G = weight of the oil sample to be tested, in grams
Precision
The permissible difference between two results for the sample is shown in the following table
Permissible Difference | Acid Number
0.02 g | Up to 0.1 g
0.05 g | From 0.1 - 1 g
0.1 g | More than 1 g
